newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks end down,take rest from recent rally.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks end down,take rest from recent rally.

text.p: Mexican stocks broke with a record-breaking run Monday and closed down on what dealers said was light profit taking.

"The market took profits at moderate volume while awaiting the outcome of (Tuesday's) primary Cetes auction. The consensus forecast is that rates will increase," said Roberto Galvan, an equity analyst with the Bursametrica consultancy.
Final closing prices placed the blue chip IPC share index down 34.55 points, or 0.83 percent, at 4,126.30. Trading volume was lackluster at 61.8 million shares.
"The market is taking a breather," a desk trader said. "Jitters over forthcoming elections were present, but it was time for every one to sell."
Mexico will hold elections July 6 for the entire lower house of Congress, one-quarter of the Senate, mayor of Mexico City and several state governors.
Dealers said May inflation data showing that the Consumer Price Index rose by 0.91 percent in May had little impact on the market.
A previous Reuters forecast of ten Mexico City financial firms had an average forecast increase of 0.92 percent for the index.
"The (inflation) data had little effect as it was exactly in line with predictions," a desk trader said.
Financial firm Bancomer weighed down most on the market. Dealers said forecast increases in primary rates encouraged profit-taking on the B series after it had gained 18 percent last week.
Bancomer's B shares slid 13 centavos (2 cents) to 3.37 pesos, (42 cents), while its A class shares ended off 7 centavos (1 cent) to 1.86 pesos (23 cents.)
Telecommunications company Telmex succumbed to profit taking and its L shares ended down 18 centavos (2 cents) to 18.62 pesos ($2.33).
The Dow Jones, meanwhile, climbed 42.72 points to a new record close of 7,478.50.
The broad market matched the declines posted by blue chips. Of a total of 108 stocks traded, decliners outpaced gainers by 58 to 23.
